title: MitoReID identifies epicatechin as a cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor
summary: A deep-learning system called MitoReID classified drug mechanisms from time-resolved mitochondrial morphology and membrane-potential images. Among its natural-compound predictions, it nominated epicatechin as a COX-2 inhibitor; the authors report in-vitro follow-up including COX-2 activity, cellular thermal-shift and surface-plasmon-resonance assays. This is a target-mechanism finding, not evidence of clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: MitoReID, deep-learning re-identification model using an Inflated 3D ResNet backbone on temporal mitochondrial images
organization: Zhejiang University; Zhejiang Lab; Zhejiang Chinese Medical University; Harvard University; Karolinska Institute; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Among its natural-compound predictions, it nominated epicatechin as a COX-2 inhibitor; the authors report in-vitro follow-up including COX-2 activity, cellular thermal-shift and surface-plasmon-resonance assays.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is biochemical/in-vitro and does not establish therapeutic efficacy or safety. MitoReID's six unseen-drug mechanism predictions are a separate task; the epicatechin COX-2 result is the specific new mechanistic finding recorded here. Full publisher page was cookie-blocked, but the primary PubMed record and publisher-indexed article text/extended-data caption were read.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked mechanisms of action for compounds by matching learned time-dependent mitochondrial phenotypes against reference drugs; the model nominated COX-2 inhibition for epicatechin, which was tested in vitro.
